styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Markets, music, craft shops and the city's buzzing street life.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Rolex chapati rolls, luwombo and grilled tilapia by the lake.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Green hills, botanical gardens and a boat ride on Lake Victoria.

stays.why: Quiet, leafy hill close to the centre; many embassies, cafés and mid-range to upscale hotels.
Central and walkable to the market, shops and offices; good mix of budget and business hotels.
Relaxed suburb with a popular mall, restaurants and easy rides to the centre.
On Lake Victoria; resorts and lake views, but 20–40 minutes by car from the centre.

food: Start with a rolex: a chapati rolled with eggs and vegetables, a cheap street breakfast or lunch.
Try luwombo (meat or chicken steamed in banana leaves) and matoke at a local restaurant.
Eat grilled tilapia by Lake Victoria in Munyonyo or at lakeside spots; check the price per fish first.
For cheap eats, look for local cafeterias serving beans, rice and posho; a meal is often a few thousand UGX.
Drink bottled or filtered water, and be cautious with raw salads and street food if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Add a day for the Uganda Museum and the Kasubi Tombs area (check opening hours on the day).
Take a boat trip on Lake Victoria or visit the Uganda Wildlife Education Centre in Entebbe.
Shop for crafts and fabrics at the National Theatre craft market and Owino market with a local guide.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the markets, food and nightlife, with time for a lake or garden break; add a night for day trips.

month_notes: January: warm and fairly dry, about 13 rain days. Good for walking and markets.
February: the driest-feeling month, around 15 rain days. Expect hot afternoons.
March: rains pick up, about 21 rain days. Carry a rain jacket and plan indoor stops.
April: the wettest month, about 26 rain days. Expect heavy afternoon showers and muddy roads.
May: still very wet, about 25 rain days. Short trips and indoor sights work best.
June: drier, about 19 rain days. Comfortable highs near 25°C.
July: one of the driest months, about 13 rain days. Good for outdoor plans.
August: showers return, about 20 rain days. Mornings are often clearer.
September: wet again, about 23 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
October: rainy, about 24 rain days. Pack waterproofs and quick-dry shoes.
November: the wettest stretch, about 25 rain days. Allow extra time for traffic in rain.
December: drier, about 20 rain days. Warm days near 26°C and busy holiday mood.

climate_guide.summary: Kampala sits near the equator: warm days, mild nights and rain in every month, heaviest from March to May and October to November.

items.title: Warm days, mild nights
items.text: Highs stay around 25–28°C all year and lows around 17–19°C. Light layers are enough.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Every month has rain days, from about 13 in January and July to 26 in April.

items.title: Wettest months
items.text: April, May, October and November are the rainiest. Expect short, heavy afternoon showers.

items.title: Drier windows
items.text: January, February and July have the fewest rain days. Still carry a rain jacket.

items.title: Rain and traffic
items.text: Heavy rain slows traffic and floods some roads. Build extra time into rides in wet months.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a rain jacket or umbrella, quick-dry shoes and mosquito repellent for evenings.

transit.best: Use Uber, Bolt or SafeBoda for most trips; matatus are cheap but crowded.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail in the city.
Fixed routes from Old Taxi Park and other stages; fares roughly UGX 1,000–3,000. Cheap but crowded and slow in traffic.
Fast but risky. Agree the fare first, usually UGX 3,000–20,000 in town. App bodas like SafeBoda include helmets.
Uber, Bolt, Faras and SafeBoda work in Kampala. Special-hire taxis rarely use meters; agree a fare, often UGX 15,000–20,000 for central trips.
Driving is possible but hectic. Traffic is heavy and rain slows it further.
Fine by day in central areas. Use rides at night and in heavy rain.
